name: Frank Zappa
milestone_by_age_26: Released Freak Out! with the Mothers of Invention on June 27, 1966 at age 25, one of rock music's first concept albums and one of the earliest double debut albums.
early_history_summary: Zappa was born in Baltimore to a Sicilian-American family; his father was a chemist in the defense industry. He began playing drums at 12, switched to guitar, and developed eclectic tastes spanning R&B, doo-wop, and modern classical composers like Varese. In the early 1960s he ran Studio Z in Cucamonga, composing film soundtracks and experimenting with tape manipulation, before joining the Soul Giants in 1965, which became the Mothers of Invention.
family_context_summary: Born to Francis Vincent Zappa, a chemist and mathematician who worked in the defense industry, and Rose Marie Colimore. The family moved frequently due to his father's work, living in Maryland, Florida, and California. His father brought lab equipment home, exposing young Zappa to mercury and scientific materials.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a chemist/mathematician in the defense industry, not music-related.
primary_early_advantage_tags: LA music scene, Studio Z access, counterculture wave, Captain Beefheart collaboration
evidence_summary: Zappa grew up in a peripatetic Italian-American family; his father was a defense-industry chemist. He began drumming at 12, developed an unusually eclectic musical taste (Varese, R&B, doo-wop), and by his early twenties was running Studio Z in Cucamonga with a 5-track recorder, composing film soundtracks and experimenting with tape manipulation. The 1960s LA music scene provided a structural wave, and his collaboration with Captain Beefheart and the underground scene gave him peer network access. His debut album Freak Out! was released in June 1966 at age 25.
starting_point: Born in Baltimore, Maryland in 1940 to an Italian-American family; father was a chemist/mathematician in the defense industry, mother was Rose Marie Colimore.
current_position: Died on December 4, 1993 at age 52; legendary American composer, guitarist, and bandleader of the Mothers of Invention, with over 60 albums released.

name: Bryan Ferry
milestone_by_age_26: Released Roxy Music's self-titled debut album on June 16, 1972 at age 26, which reached No. 10 on the UK album charts and established the band's presence in the British music scene.
early_history_summary: Ferry was born to a working-class family in Washington, County Durham; his father was a farm labourer who looked after pit ponies. He studied fine art at Newcastle University from 1964 to 1968 under Richard Hamilton, played in bands during university, then moved to London in 1968 and taught art at Holland Park School while pursuing music. He formed Roxy Music in November 1970 and signed to Island Records in May 1972.

evidence_summary: Ferry came from a working-class family in County Durham; his father was a farm labourer. He studied fine art at Newcastle University under Richard Hamilton, which gave him an art-school sensibility unusual in rock. After moving to London in 1968 and teaching art, he formed Roxy Music in 1970 with key collaborators including Brian Eno, Andy Mackay, and Phil Manzanera. The band's debut album was released in June 1972 when Ferry was 26, reaching No. 10 in the UK. The early 1970s London glam/art rock scene provided a structural wave.
